correctness.rationale: Generated all independent triples from the nine-cycle and isolate: 30 cycle-only plus 27 isolate-containing triples, with 138+360=498 disjointness edges. Explicit least-label six-coloring gives chi<=6. Independent DSATUR/backtracking enumerator exhaustively canonicalized five-colorings (not a timeout) in 122153 recursive states and found none, giving chi>=6. Source witness file contains five-colorings of six dihedral vertex-orbit representatives of sizes 9,18,9,3,9,9; independent verification transported them under all 18 graph automorphisms and checked every edge and all 57 vertex deletions. Three explicit disjoint triples give clique >=3, while four would require twelve of ten labels. This is a complete finite proof conditional on transparent deterministic exact code; no extrapolation to larger cycles.

originality.rationale: Arana–Haxell–Kaiser–Stehlik 2026 define precisely these G-stable Kneser graphs; their Theorem 1.2 excludes short cycles, Theorem 1.4 gives asymptotic C_{n-1} plus isolated vertex tightness without an explicit first k=3 boundary, and Conjecture 1.3 asks for the general statement. Schrijver 1978 vertex-criticality treats a single cycle and cannot be transplanted to the 57-vertex isolate-extended graph (classical SG(10,3) has 50 vertices). The full preprint notes computational support; unpublished prior checking of this specific example remains possible.
residual_risks: Arana et al explicitly mention unspecified computational tests; a prior computation of this exact first boundary graph may exist, though not located as a published theorem.
Machine-assisted finite proof relies on completeness of transparent canonical color search and correctness of witness parsing; independent implementation matched the 122153-state count.
Nothing proved for cycle lengths beyond nine, k>3 or edge-criticality.

value.rationale: This is the first k=3 cycle-plus-isolated-vertex case at the sharp 4k-3 boundary of a published G-stable Kneser chromatic conjecture, beyond the source theorem excluding cycles through 4k-4. Establishing vertex criticality and a strict clique/chromatic gap for the fully specified natural 57-vertex graph is a motivated exact cutoff, not an arbitrary graph invariant.

final_claim: The graph whose 57 vertices are independent triples of C_9 disjoint union K_1, with adjacency by disjointness of triples, has 498 edges, chromatic number 6, clique number 3, and after deletion of any one vertex has chromatic number exactly 5.
